changelog.change: The campaign's baseline measurement is recorded: 1712 of the 1923 official suite cases convert, 211 are refused, and 107 official-reference comparisons fail.
The machine-readable expectation manifest is added, so every case's expected verdict at every stage is recorded rather than re-derived by hand.

Closed: the harness now validates official references for action-bearing and stochastic cases (PR #337), so the harness-side limits 'scheduled actions not executed' and 'stochastic ensemble not evaluated' are gone.
The suite no longer exercises the algebraic-rule and assigned-stoichiometry refusals: the campaign resolved those cases (PRs #355 and #366). The refusals themselves still exist in the Atomizer.

Opened: two harness-side classes were named, so the measurement limits 'random event execution' and 'reference does not track variable' are now visible as such instead of being counted as Atomizer limitations (PR #359).

Reduced: a fast reaction is lowered to its pseudo steady state instead of being refused (PR #370), and several simultaneous events execute in the order the specification defines (PR #371). The official-reference failure count is zero.

Closed: a reference that names a reaction's rate is now compared, because the Atomizer states the rate as a zero-argument function and the harness maps the reference's quantity onto it (PR #378); and a boundary species is now honoured by the direct SSA path, so the reference's value for it is compared rather than skipped (PR #380). The event limit 'an event the Atomizer cannot lower, or cannot order' shrinks by one case: an event group whose priority is read from the model state is now ordered by the priority it has at the execution instant (PR #376).

Corrected three previously unclassified cause/owner labels without changing verdicts or stage counts: semantic/00950 is MathML infinity, semantic/00951 is a non-finite parameter approximation, and stochastic/00028 and stochastic/00032 are scheduled-action phase-boundary comparison limits owned by the harness.

compartment:unsupported-spatial-dimensio.bng3_does: The Atomizer refuses the compartment and says why: "Compartment \"C\" has spatialDimensions 7; BNG3 does not support spatialDimensions values greater than 3." It also refuses a negative dimension and, for a Level 2 model, any value outside 0 through 3.
compartment:unsupported-spatial-dimensio.citation: SBML Level 3 Version 2 Core Sec. 4.5.2, Sec. 4.5.4
compartment:unsupported-spatial-dimensio.reducible: No, not as a compartment. BNGL compartments carry a volume; a compartment with a fractal or higher dimension has no BNGL counterpart, and the unit selection Sec. 4.5.4 describes cannot be expressed.
compartment:unsupported-spatial-dimensio.sbml_requires: SBML Level 3 Version 2 Core Sec. 4.5.2 lets a compartment declare any floating-point spatialDimensions value, and Sec. 4.5.4 uses that value to choose between the model's volumeUnits, areaUnits and lengthUnits.
compartment:unsupported-spatial-dimensio.title: A compartment with more than three spatial dimensions

events:state-trigger-not-schedulable.bng3_does: The Atomizer refuses the event and says why: "trigger is not a simple time threshold (state-dependent triggers cannot be scheduled)", or, when the trigger names an identifier that is not a legal SBML SId, that the identifier "contains a character outside the SBML SId class and cannot be matched".
events:state-trigger-not-schedulable.citation: SBML Level 3 Version 2 Core Sec. 4.12.2, Sec. 4.12.7
events:state-trigger-not-schedulable.reducible: Yes, in two directions. A trigger the native event runtime can evaluate is lowered rather than refused (PR #328, 2026-10-21); an identifier that is not a legal SId is a source defect the user can fix by renaming it, and the diagnostic says so.
events:state-trigger-not-schedulable.sbml_requires: SBML Level 3 Version 2 Core Sec. 4.12.2 requires the Trigger to be evaluated against the model's current state, and Sec. 4.12.7 requires the event to be executed when the trigger becomes true.
events:state-trigger-not-schedulable.title: A state trigger the runtime cannot schedule

events:untranslated.bng3_does: The Atomizer lowers an event whose trigger is a constant time threshold to a scheduled BNGL action and refuses the rest: it reports "N SBML event(s) parsed; M fixed-time event(s) lowered to scheduled actions, while K state-dependent or non-constant event(s) remain untranslated", and the case is not claimed to be supported. The refusal names the specific condition, for example "state-triggered SBML events require stochastic jump scheduling", "the model's algebraic rule is not applied, so the event's trigger cannot be evaluated", "volume change can cause the state trigger to re-enter within the simulation horizon" or "trigger time ... does not reduce to a constant".
events:untranslated.citation: SBML Level 3 Version 2 Core Sec. 4.12, Sec. 4.12.2, Sec. 4.12.3, Sec. 4.12.7
events:untranslated.reducible: Partly reduced, and the work is continuing. A state trigger the native event runtime can evaluate is now lowered (PR #328, 2026-10-21) and several simultaneous events execute in the order the specification defines (PR #371, 2026-10-21), and a simultaneous group whose priority is read from the model state is now ordered by the priority it has at the execution instant, which SBML L3V2 Core Sec. 4.12.3 requires (PR #376, 2026-10-21). What remains needs a trigger value the engine does not poll, a trigger whose value depends on a construct the Atomizer does not apply, or an event whose effect is not a scheduled action.
events:untranslated.sbml_requires: SBML Level 3 Version 2 Core Sec. 4.12 defines an Event as a two-phase operation: a Trigger (Sec. 4.12.2) decides when the event may fire, and the execution phase applies the EventAssignments (Sec. 4.12.5). Sec. 4.12.7 says the order in which events occur is resolved, that this order can be significant for a simulation's outcome, and that an event may carry a special priority through a Priority subobject (Sec. 4.12.3).
events:untranslated.title: An event the Atomizer cannot lower, or cannot order

fast-reaction:no-fast-equilibrium-solve.bng3_does: The Atomizer reduces a fast reaction to its pseudo steady state where it can (PR #370, 2026-10-21) and refuses the remainder, saying that it treats such a reaction as an ordinary reaction and that this changes the trajectory.
fast-reaction:no-fast-equilibrium-solve.citation: SBML Level 3 Version 1 Core Sec. 4.11; SBML Level 3 Version 2 Core Sec. 4.11
fast-reaction:no-fast-equilibrium-solve.reducible: Largely reduced already: the reduction closed most of these cases. The remainder needs a fast reaction whose pseudo steady state cannot be written as a BNGL rule.
fast-reaction:no-fast-equilibrium-solve.sbml_requires: SBML Level 3 Version 1 Core Sec. 4.11 asks that software tools use a pseudo steady-state approximation for the set of reactions whose fast attribute is true. SBML Level 3 Version 2 removed the fast attribute (Sec. 4.11), so a Level 3 Version 2 model says nothing about fast reactions.
fast-reaction:no-fast-equilibrium-solve.title: A fast reaction whose pseudo steady state cannot be used

mathml:non-finite-parameter-approximatio.bng3_does: The case source validates with libSBML, but parameter values include infinity and NaN. The writer emits finite placeholder numbers to produce a diagnostic artifact and marks the conversion unsupported; these placeholders do not preserve the source values.
mathml:non-finite-parameter-approximatio.citation: SBML Level 3 Version 2 Core Sec. 3.1.4; MathML 2 Sec. 4.2.3
mathml:non-finite-parameter-approximatio.reducible: No within BNG3's finite numeric state; conversion must keep refusing rather than treating the emitted finite placeholder as equivalent.
mathml:non-finite-parameter-approximatio.sbml_requires: The source values use non-finite numeric values, which are distinct from any finite value. A finite-double target cannot preserve them by substituting an arbitrary finite parameter.
mathml:non-finite-parameter-approximatio.title: A non-finite parameter value is replaced by a finite diagnostic placeholder

harness:scheduled-action-phase-boundary.bng3_does: The source model converts, round-trips, and passes the independent trajectory comparison. The official reference grid includes the exact scheduled-action boundary, where the official convention reports the assignment as already applied while the native action dispatcher exposes the pre-assignment phase value. The point-wise reference comparison therefore remains unsupported.
harness:scheduled-action-phase-boundary.citation: SBML Level 3 Version 2 Core Sec. 4.12.5, Sec. 4.12.7; campaign reference-comparison contract
harness:scheduled-action-phase-boundary.reducible: Yes, in the comparison contract: sample the post-event value at the defined boundary, or compare according to the event execution phase. This is a harness/runtime observation-boundary issue, not an Atomizer refusal.
harness:scheduled-action-phase-boundary.sbml_requires: SBML event execution applies EventAssignments when the event fires; the reporting convention at an event time must distinguish pre-event from post-event state.
harness:scheduled-action-phase-boundary.title: The official reference samples a scheduled-action phase boundary

harness:random-event-execution.bng3_does: Nothing is refused: the model converts and the engine executes the events in the order the specification defines. The harness cannot compare point-wise, because the reference is one draw of a random order and no deterministic simulator reproduces it point-wise.
harness:random-event-execution.citation: SBML Level 3 Version 2 Core Sec. 4.12.3, Sec. 4.12.7
harness:random-event-execution.reducible: Yes, on the measurement side: the comparison has to be distributional rather than point-wise, or the reference has to pin the order. It is a measurement limit, not a limitation of the Atomizer.
harness:random-event-execution.sbml_requires: SBML Level 3 Version 2 Core Sec. 4.12.3 and Sec. 4.12.7 define the order in which simultaneously triggered events are executed; a case that draws the events in a random order is a valid instance of that semantics.
harness:random-event-execution.title: The official reference is one draw of a random execution order

harness:reference-does-not-track-variabl.bng3_does: Nothing was refused: the model converted, but the direct SSA path decremented and incremented a boundary species like any other, so the species' value drifted away from the value the reference reports. The direct SSA path now skips a constant species in its state update — the propensity is untouched, so a boundary species still contributes its amount to the rate law it appears in — and the batched accelerator path does the same, so every engine agrees.
harness:reference-does-not-track-variabl.closed_by: PR #380, validated 2026-10-21, first measured as closed on 2026-10-21
harness:reference-does-not-track-variabl.reducible: Closed: the direct SSA path and the batched accelerator now honour a boundary species (PR #380, 2026-10-21), so the model's value matches the reference's and the cases are compared rather than skipped.
harness:reference-does-not-track-variabl.resolved_note: Closed by PR #380, validated 2026-10-21: the direct SSA path no longer decrements or increments a boundary species, so the model's value matches the official reference and the three cases are compared instead of skipped. The defect had been a symptom of the engine honouring a boundary species in three of its four engines. First measured as closed on 2026-10-21.
harness:reference-does-not-track-variabl.sbml_requires: SBML Level 3 Version 2 Core Sec. 4.6.6 lets a species carry the boundaryCondition attribute, in which case the species is a boundary rather than an integrated quantity.
harness:reference-does-not-track-variabl.title: The official reference does not report a boundary species

harness:scheduled-actions-not-executed.bng3_does: Nothing was refused. The harness's in-memory reference runner could not execute actions on the official output grid, so it reported the case as unsupported.
harness:scheduled-actions-not-executed.citation: SBML Level 3 Version 2 Core Sec. 4.12 (scheduled events)
harness:scheduled-actions-not-executed.closed_by: PR #337, validated 2026-10-20, first measured as closed on 2026-10-21
harness:scheduled-actions-not-executed.reducible: Closed: the harness now validates official references for action-bearing cases (PR #337, 2026-10-20), so these cases are compared rather than skipped.
harness:scheduled-actions-not-executed.resolved_note: Closed by PR #337, validated 2026-10-20: the harness now validates official references for action-bearing cases, so these cases are compared rather than skipped. First measured as closed on 2026-10-21.
harness:scheduled-actions-not-executed.sbml_requires: Nothing: this was a limit of the measurement, not of the model.
harness:scheduled-actions-not-executed.title: The reference runner could not execute a model with actions

harness:stochastic-ensemble-not-evaluate.bng3_does: Nothing was refused. The harness reported that official stochastic conformance requires a repeated-run mean and standard deviation, which it did not evaluate.
harness:stochastic-ensemble-not-evaluate.citation: SBML Level 3 Version 2 Core Sec. 4.11.7 (stochastic reaction semantics)
harness:stochastic-ensemble-not-evaluate.closed_by: PR #337, validated 2026-10-20, first measured as closed on 2026-10-21
harness:stochastic-ensemble-not-evaluate.reducible: Closed: the harness now evaluates the official stochastic references (PR #337, validated 2026-10-20), so these cases are compared rather than skipped.
harness:stochastic-ensemble-not-evaluate.resolved_note: Closed by PR #337, validated 2026-10-20: the harness now evaluates the official stochastic references, so these cases are compared rather than skipped. First measured as closed on 2026-10-21.
harness:stochastic-ensemble-not-evaluate.sbml_requires: Nothing: this was a limit of the measurement, not of the model.
harness:stochastic-ensemble-not-evaluate.title: The official reference needed an ensemble the harness did not run

mathml:infinity.bng3_does: The Atomizer reports "<infinity> constant encountered in math; the source is valid SBML (validation rule 10202 permits <infinity>), but an infinite value cannot be represented in BNG3's finite-double model, so it is emitted as a large finite value and the model is not claimed to be supported".
mathml:infinity.citation: SBML Level 3 Version 2 Core Sec. 3.1.5, Sec. 3.4.1
mathml:infinity.reducible: Only by changing what BNG3's value domain is. The source is valid SBML and the boundary is BNG3's finite-double model, not a conversion defect; a large finite stand-in is an approximation, so the case is refused rather than claimed.
mathml:infinity.sbml_requires: SBML Level 3 Version 2 Core Sec. 3.4.1 permits the MathML infinity constant in a model's formulas, and Sec. 3.1.5 makes positive infinity a value of the double type.
mathml:infinity.title: An infinite constant

mathml:not-a-number.bng3_does: The Atomizer reports "<notanumber> constant encountered in math; the source is valid SBML (validation rule 10202 permits <notanumber>), but a not-a-number value cannot be represented in BNG3's finite-double model, so the model is not claimed to be supported".
mathml:not-a-number.citation: SBML Level 3 Version 2 Core Sec. 3.1.5, Sec. 3.4.1
mathml:not-a-number.reducible: Only by changing BNG3's value domain. There is no finite value that stands for not-a-number, so no approximation is offered.
mathml:not-a-number.sbml_requires: SBML Level 3 Version 2 Core Sec. 3.4.1 permits the MathML notanumber constant in a model's formulas, and Sec. 3.1.5 makes not-a-number a value of the double type.
mathml:not-a-number.title: A not-a-number constant

other.bng3_does: The Atomizer refuses the case and reports the reason; the campaign's classification records it as "other" because no known construct class matches.
other.citation: SBML Level 3 Version 2 Core, the section the case's own reason names
other.reducible: Unknown until each reason is read. This bucket is a request to extend the taxonomy, not a claim that the cases are alike.
other.sbml_requires: No single construct: each case is refused for a reason the campaign's cause taxonomy has no label for yet.
other.title: Refusals the cause taxonomy does not yet name

package:fbc.bng3_does: The Atomizer reports that the package is declared and that the affected structure is missing from the converted model, and it says why the model is out of scope: "This is a constraint-based flux-balance model, not a kinetic time-course model."
package:fbc.citation: SBML Level 3 Package for Flux Balance Constraints (FBC) Version 1 Release 3; the Core itself is SBML Level 3 Version 2 Core Sec. 4.11.7 and Sec. 4.12.7
package:fbc.reducible: No, not as a time course. BNG3 has no flux-balance solver, so a flux-balance model is not convertible; the honest boundary is to refuse it and to say that it is a different kind of model.
package:fbc.sbml_requires: The SBML Level 3 Package for Flux Balance Constraints (FBC) adds goals and constraints to a model. A model that carries FBC elements is a constraint-based model, not a kinetic time course, so the Core's reaction semantics (Sec. 4.11.7) and event semantics (Sec. 4.12.7) do not give it a trajectory to compare.
package:fbc.title: The fbc package: a flux-balance model, not a time course

reference:no-result-mapping.bng3_does: The Atomizer states each reaction's rate as a zero-argument function in the generated model, and the harness maps a reference variable naming a reaction onto that function, so the quantity is compared. A rate that cannot be stated in the model's own symbols states no rate, and the refusal is preserved rather than approximated.
reference:no-result-mapping.closed_by: PR #378, validated 2026-10-21, first measured as closed on 2026-10-21
reference:no-result-mapping.reducible: Closed: the Atomizer states a reaction's rate as a zero-argument function (PR #378, 2026-10-21), and the harness maps the reference's reaction id onto it, so these cases are compared rather than skipped. The boundary that remains is a rate that cannot be stated in the model's own symbols, which is still refused.
reference:no-result-mapping.resolved_note: Closed by PR #378, validated 2026-10-21: the Atomizer states each reaction's rate as a zero-argument function and the harness maps a reference variable naming a reaction onto it, so the twenty-two cases are compared against the official reference instead of being skipped. First measured as closed on 2026-10-21.
reference:no-result-mapping.sbml_requires: SBML Level 3 Version 2 Core Sec. 4.11.8 says the id of a Reaction may be used in a MathML formula and then represents that reaction's rate. The official SBML Test Suite's results file for such a case reports that rate as the quantity to compare.
reference:no-result-mapping.title: The official reference names a quantity BNG3 cannot observe

reference:not-applicable.bng3_does: Nothing is refused and nothing is claimed. The case is recorded as having no official reference, which is not a limitation of the Atomizer and not a defect.
reference:not-applicable.citation: the official SBML Test Suite's own case notes; no Core section applies
reference:not-applicable.reducible: Not applicable. The official suite defines no reference for these cases, so there is no comparison to make and no work to do.
reference:not-applicable.sbml_requires: Nothing in the Core applies: the official suite itself records that the case defines no official time-course reference, so there is nothing to compare against.
reference:not-applicable.title: The suite says the case has no official time-course reference

rules:algebraic-not-applied.bng3_does: The Atomizer still refuses such a model: it reports "N algebraic rule(s) present; these are implicit DAE constraints with no BNGL equivalent and are not applied". The official suite no longer reaches this refusal, so the limitation itself is still open while the suite no longer exercises it.
rules:algebraic-not-applied.reducible: Yes: the campaign resolved the suite's algebraic-rule cases by carrying the rule as an assignment (PR #355, 2026-10-20). The general implicit-DAE boundary is still open.
rules:algebraic-not-applied.resolved_note: The refusal still exists in the Atomizer; the official suite no longer reaches it, because the campaign resolved the suite's algebraic-rule cases by carrying the rule as an assignment (PR #355, 2026-10-20). The general implicit-DAE boundary is still open, so the construct is recorded as no longer exercised rather than closed.
rules:algebraic-not-applied.sbml_requires: SBML Level 3 Version 2 Core Sec. 4.9.2 defines an algebraic rule as an equation that is neither an assignment of a model variable nor a rate of change, and says that in the context of a simulation algebraic rules are in effect at all times.
rules:algebraic-not-applied.title: An algebraic rule is not applied

sbml-writer:unrepresentable-function.bng3_does: The C++ SBML writer serializes the call back out, but the engine cannot execute it: it reports "SBML math function \"delay\" is not losslessly representable in the BNG3 engine/libRoadRunner path: the C++ SBML writer serializes the call, but neither the BNG3 engine nor libRoadRunner can evaluate SBML delay semantics".
sbml-writer:unrepresentable-function.reducible: No, not in the engine. BNG3 has no delayed-history semantics and libRoadRunner rejects a model that uses delay at all, so a model that needs them cannot be executed by either engine; the writer boundary itself was already removed.
sbml-writer:unrepresentable-function.sbml_requires: SBML Level 3 Version 2 Core Sec. 3.4.6 defines the delay and rateOf operators as csymbol elements with a fixed definitionURL, and requires a reader to give delay(x, d) the value x had at time t - d.
sbml-writer:unrepresentable-function.title: A math function the engine cannot execute

stoichiometry:assigned-stoichiometry-unr.bng3_does: The Atomizer still reports that the stoichiometry "is assigned by ..., whose value could not be resolved to a number at initialization". The official suite no longer reaches this refusal, so the limitation itself is still open while the suite no longer exercises it.
stoichiometry:assigned-stoichiometry-unr.citation: SBML Level 3 Version 2 Core Sec. 4.9, Sec. 4.11.3
stoichiometry:assigned-stoichiometry-unr.reducible: Yes: the campaign resolved the suite's cases by carrying the assigned value through the parameter's state (PR #366, 2026-10-21). A symbol that still cannot be resolved at initialization remains refused.
stoichiometry:assigned-stoichiometry-unr.resolved_note: The refusal still exists in the Atomizer; the official suite no longer reaches it, because the campaign resolved the suite's cases by carrying the assigned value through the parameter's state (PR #366, 2026-10-21). A symbol that still cannot be resolved at initialization remains refused.
stoichiometry:assigned-stoichiometry-unr.sbml_requires: SBML Level 3 Version 2 Core Sec. 4.11.3 gives a speciesReference id the meaning of a model-level symbol whose value is that reference's stoichiometry, and Sec. 4.9 lets a rule determine that symbol's value.
stoichiometry:assigned-stoichiometry-unr.title: An assigned stoichiometry that could not be resolved

stoichiometry:unsupported.bng3_does: The Atomizer still refuses such a reaction and reports that it has unsupported stoichiometry. The official suite no longer reaches this refusal, so the limitation itself is still open while the suite no longer exercises it.
stoichiometry:unsupported.reducible: Only by extending BNGL's reaction semantics: a negative or fractional stoichiometry has no BNGL counterpart, and substituting a rounded count would change the chemistry.
stoichiometry:unsupported.resolved_note: The refusal still exists in the Atomizer; the official suite no longer reaches it. The boundary is only reducible by extending BNGL's reaction semantics: a negative or fractional stoichiometry has no BNGL counterpart, and substituting a rounded count would change the chemistry.
stoichiometry:unsupported.sbml_requires: SBML Level 3 Version 2 Core Sec. 4.11.3 lets a speciesReference carry any stoichiometry, including a negative or fractional one.
stoichiometry:unsupported.title: A reaction with a stoichiometry BNGL cannot express

harness:stochastic-ensemble-budget-not-c.title: Projected stochastic work exceeds the comparison-planning threshold
harness:stochastic-ensemble-budget-not-c.sbml_requires: The official stochastic reference specifies an ensemble size and reports an ensemble outcome; comparison requires the harness to execute that ensemble and evaluate its statistics.
harness:stochastic-ensemble-budget-not-c.citation: DSMTS user guide and the pinned official test case settings
harness:stochastic-ensemble-budget-not-c.bng3_does: The SBML model converts. A fixed-seed CPU probe projects ensemble work above the configured planning threshold, so the harness marks the official comparison not comparable. The projection is an estimate; it is not an enforced cap or a runtime guarantee.
harness:stochastic-ensemble-budget-not-c.reducible: Yes, on the harness side: improve planning or execution so the specified ensemble can be evaluated, then compare it without changing the official statistics or thresholds.

note: The narrative half of docs/ATOMIZER_LIMITATIONS.md. The counts, the case ids, the sides and the recorded measurement come from the expectation manifest (provenance/sbml-campaign/expectations.json); this file records what each construct is, what the specification requires, what BNG3 does instead, whether the limitation is reducible, and when it was first recorded. It is the one part of the document that is maintained by hand, and the generator checks it against the manifest on every run.
